title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: Chronos-2 is best on three load datasets when future covariates are available or accurate, but degrades as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet is more robust.
why_relevant: Directly tests foundation models on load with known-future weather of varying quality, which is our oracle vs forecast regime question.

title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)
claim: In a preregistered 960-day GB day-ahead backtest, giving honestly timed weather forecasts to Chronos-2, Timestral-209M and a weekly-lag regression cuts error by roughly a quarter to a third, but not for TimesFM 2.5 once a batching leak was corrected.
why_relevant: Same design as our primary comparison (zero-shot foundation model with weather vs lag regression), on hourly-type national load, but day-ahead rather than week-ahead.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: Over 32 live days, adding the same weather covariates cut error by 37-51% for ten foundation models on matched races across price, wind, solar and load in six European zones.
why_relevant: Live benchmark with frozen weather inputs and foundation models with and without covariates, including load; day-ahead and European.

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
claim: On four PJM extreme-cold events, day-ahead 90% intervals lose coverage and no calibrator chosen without the target event restores it; leave-one-event-out transfer evaluation overstates coverage.
why_relevant: Preregistered probabilistic PJM load benchmark with temperature-based calibration, though day-ahead and about intervals, not foundation models.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load, Chronos-2 gains a lot from fine-tuning and is strong at short horizons, but zero-shot it trails task-specific deep models.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with covariates on US ISO load, the model in our primary comparison.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Rank-16 LoRA cuts MOIRAI Large's error by 7.5% on average across four load aggregation levels; Chronos-2 is better pretrained but gains less from adaptation.
why_relevant: Foundation models on electrical load, but fine-tuned and the horizon and covariates are not stated in the abstract.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
claim: Open-weights 102M and 256M models that use past and known-future covariates and rank near the top of GIFT-Eval and fev-bench, with covariates adding about 6 points of skill.
why_relevant: Known-future covariates and an electricity-demand result; listed among models we can wrap.

title: Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models
claim: Four open-weight probabilistic forecasters of 5M to 209M parameters that take known-future covariates natively and are reported to lead GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench.
why_relevant: Runs on CPU, takes temperature as known-future input, and already in our runnable models list.

title: TimesFM 3.0 (Google Research)
claim: A 330M-parameter zero-shot model natively trained for multivariate forecasting with past and known-future covariates such as weather forecasts.
why_relevant: Covariate-capable foundation model released inside our scored window, so weeks-after-weights matters.

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data
claim: On post-release data TimesFM 3 beats a classical ensemble by 16% MASE overall, but on load, prices and river flow the point-forecast advantage is not confirmed and its 80% intervals cover about 70%.
why_relevant: Leakage-aware test of a covariate-capable model that includes electricity load.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: Chronos-2 gives the lowest error in high-demand periods at area, substation and feeder level on UK and Swiss open data, ahead of LightGBM, XGBoost, statistical baselines and Chronos-Bolt.
why_relevant: Compares Chronos-2 with gradient-boosted regressors on load, but at distribution level and short horizons.
query: site:arxiv.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: An adaptive GAM with state-space updating that aggregates several weather forecast providers improves point and probabilistic load forecasts by diluting the effect of weather prediction errors.
why_relevant: Directly about using archived weather forecasts (not actuals) as load covariates, matching our forecast regime; no foundation model involved.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one university building, TimesFM 3.0 with covariates cuts MAE by about 43% against weekly seasonal naive, but paired daily tests show no clear advantage over XGBoost, and weather covariates use retrospective observations.
why_relevant: Compares TimesFM 3.0 with covariates against XGBoost on the same inputs, but for one building, day-ahead, with observed weather.
query: site:arxiv.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act requirements: results from a 41-day live challenge on German transmission-grid load
claim: A deterministic local pipeline with calendar and weather covariates beat the ENTSO-E day-ahead forecast over 41 live days and was competitive with Chronos-2.
why_relevant: Live out-of-sample load challenge with weather covariates and a foundation-model comparison; day-ahead only.

title: Choosing Load Forecasting Methods by Horizon, History and Hour: Reserve and Imbalance Evidence from Four Grids (companion data and code)
claim: A reproduction package with a pre-specified protocol and a log of deviations compares rolling-origin load forecasts at horizons of 1 to 180 days and hourly day-ahead forecasts on four national grids, with online selection and conformal intervals.
why_relevant: Has a pre-specified protocol with deviations logged and covers horizons that include a week, but the record does not say which models or covariates were used (not confirmed beyond the record text).
query: site:zenodo.org electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 respond to a covariate like an observational regression, so their what-if answers are confounded.
why_relevant: Bears on how far to trust the covariate response of the models we run; synthetic and physical systems, not load.

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Turkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
claim: An archive of 759 training runs of multi-horizon national demand models using calendar, holiday and temperature information.
why_relevant: Multi-horizon national load with temperature; the record has no headline result, so the claim is thin.

title: Online Conditional Vine Copulas: Forecasting Electricity Demand
claim: An online covariate-conditioned vine copula model beats unconditional benchmarks on GB net-demand across five regions and updates cheaply.
why_relevant: Probabilistic regional demand with covariates; horizon and weather use not stated.

title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models
claim: Chronos-2, t0-beta and TiRex-2 respond more strongly to a covariate supplied as several identical channels, and in a public energy dataset a duplicated weather station changes day-ahead forecasts; declaring the source removes the effect.
why_relevant: Bears on how temperature must be supplied to covariate models so every model sees the identical series (our rule 3).
query: site:zenodo.org TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: Timestral and Chronos-2 without covariates beat SARIMA and GBM baselines on hourly 96-hour carbon intensity in the 2025 test, but the 14-origin post-release holdout is inconclusive.
why_relevant: Preregistered hourly energy-related forecast with the same models, but carbon intensity and no covariates.

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
claim: Both models beat trained baselines on hourly 24-hour heat load with an ambient-temperature covariate, Chronos-2 slightly ahead of TabPFN-TS.
why_relevant: Hourly energy series with temperature as a known-future input, but heat load and a 24-hour horizon.

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
claim: A new tabular foundation model release that reports stronger time-series forecasting through task-specific harnesses.
why_relevant: TabPFN-TS-style forecasting with covariates may build on it; the abstract gives no load result.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
claim: How calendar covariates are encoded changes zero-shot accuracy of four covariate-aware foundation models, by up to 83% on holidays.
why_relevant: Covariate handling in foundation models of the kind we run; calendar not temperature, and not load-specific.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: Economic indicators lift a tabular foundation model's French load forecasts by about 20% at 1 to 48 months ahead.
why_relevant: Foundation model on load with covariates, but monthly and daily resolution at much longer horizons.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark on ESHED-38
claim: On 48 weekly origins over a 359-day holdout for 38 homes, Chronos-2 is the most accurate zero-shot model one day ahead and ties TimesFM-2.5 and Chronos-Bolt at one week, with the best configurations about 20-25% better than seasonal naive.
why_relevant: Weekly rolling origins and a one-week lead time with Chronos-2, but daily smart-meter data for homes in Iraq.
query: site:arxiv.org pre-registered forecasting backtest energy demand

title: IBM Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2
claim: A 385M-parameter Apache-2.0 zero-shot model ranked top among permissively licensed replicable models on GIFT-Eval as of 8 September 2026; the page does not mention covariates.
why_relevant: Open univariate forecasting model that could run on load history only.

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: A 145M-parameter open model with a full training recipe, competitive zero-shot on GIFT-Eval and TIME.
why_relevant: Open univariate foundation model; Tabby is on the FoundationForecast wrapper list.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?
claim: Compares foundation models such as TimesFM-2.5 and TabPFN variants with market-specific models for electricity price forecasting (from the title and search summary only).
why_relevant: Hourly energy price series, not load.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
claim: In a preregistered simulation on 7,200 series neither TimesFM-3 nor classical methods dominate; TimesFM-3 is never over 1.31 times the best method but gains nothing on intermittent demand.
why_relevant: Preregistered comparison of a covariate-capable model, but on simulated data with a 12-step horizon.
